Definition: adverb from G2033; seven times:--seven times.
BiblicalUsage: I take heptákis to mean seven times, nothing more and nothing less. It occurs 3 times, and Matthew and Luke show it doing ordinary work in ordinary sentences. The Bible uses plain words plainly, and this is one of them.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that heptákis matters because seven is the Bible’s number of completeness — God finished His work and rested. My position is that Scripture does not hide its meaning from honest readers.
